pollūcĭbĭlis , e, adj. polluceo, bountifully distributed; hence, in gen.,
I.sumptuous, rich, magnificent (post-class.): cena,
Macr. S. 2, 13 fin.: “victus,” Symm. Ep. 6, 71 . —Comp.: “obsonandi pollucibilior,” Tert. Jejun. 17 .—Adv.: pollūcĭbĭlĭter , sumptuously, magnificently (ante-class.): “obsonate,” Plaut. Most. 1, 1, 23 : pergraecamini, id. Fragm. ap. Fulg. Myth. 1, 2.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
